messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING — p95 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (prod, us-west-2). Threshold crossed at 2026-03-17T01:12:57Z. Alert ID: INC-2026-4302. Auto-attach: sample spans + flamegraphs.
maria: oncall here, ACKing. Joining now, pulling up traces and perf counters. @kevin @dmitri can you share any recent infra changes? :white_check_mark:
kevin: looking at traces — p50 ~ 120ms, p95 jumped from ~450ms -> ~2.1s starting ~01:11:30Z. Bulk of tail is in kernel scheduling stalls and a few long syscalls in ksoftirq. Starting span dump: ```
span_id=0x7f3 time_ms=2100 service=inference node=i-0a1b2c trace=[decode->kv_read->dispatch]
kv_read: tail latency 1500ms (many samples)
dispatch: short CPU work 30ms
```
dmitri: infra note: we rolled kernel 5.15.72->5.15.73 on a subset of nodes at 01:10Z as part of a security backport. Rollout ~20% of fleet (6/30 nodes). I'm seeing correlation in host list.
carla: customer impact: CS reports increased retries from 5 mid-market customers since ~01:15Z. Error rate up, some timeouts surface in logs. I'm messaging account reps.
maria: hypothesis list (tracked inline):
- H1: kernel scheduling regression from 5.15.73 rollout causing tail CPU stalls for inference worker threads.
- H2: KV cache prefix misses + thundering herd causing IO stalls and long syscall waits.
- H3: recent runtime runtime-2.4.1 config change (prefetch disabled) -> increased latencies for hot keys.
We should gather perf counters and isolate by host kernel version.
kevin: quick grep across traces shows hosts with high p95 all have kernel 5.15.73. Non-upgraded nodes stay low. Also noticed increased ctx-switches metrics. Sample mstats (host i-0a1b2c): ```
# sar -c 1 1
%user  %system  %iowait
8.2     4.1      0.0
```
kevin: running `sudo perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-cycles,task-clock -p $(pgrep inference_worker) -I 1000 -o /tmp/perf.out` on suspect node now. Attaching excerpt when available.
dmitri: attaching perf excerpt from i-0a1b2c (01:18Z): ```
Performance counter stats for 'pid 1234':

      1,234,567 context-switches
     98,765,432 cpu-cycles
     12.345 task-clock (msec)
```
maria: timeline so far:
- 01:10Z: kernel 5.15.73 rollout starts (6 nodes)
- 01:11:30Z: first p95 jump observed in traces
- 01:12:57Z: Pager triggered (INC-2026-4302)
- 01:14Z: CS reports retries from customers
- 01:16Z: perf + spans indicate kernel-related stalls on upgraded hosts
elaine: quick mitigation options: (A) divert traffic away from upgraded hosts via routing policy (fast), (B) rollback kernel on the 6 hosts (slower), (C) increase worker pool to absorb tails (temporary). Recommend A + C immediately.
maria: implementing mitigation A: using routing policy to drain traffic from nodes with 5.15.73. Command executed: ```
# rctl route update --cluster prod-usw2 --exclude-label kernel=5.15.73 --dry-run=false
Routing change applied, draining connections from 6 nodes.```
kevin: after routing change p95 on global front decreased to ~650ms within 90s. Not fully back to baseline but much improved. Captured post-mitigation flame: ```
span_id=0x7f3 time_ms=680 service=inference node=i-0d3f2a trace=[kv_read->dispatch]
kv_read tail samples down from 1500ms -> 120ms
```
carla: CS update: customer retries falling, no new tickets after 01:22Z. Marking customer impact as reduced but still follow-up required.
dmitri: we should still collect full perf logs and stack samples for RCA. I'll keep hosts quarantined and gather `perf record -a -g` for the window 01:08-01:22Z.
maria: assigning actions:
- dmitri: collect full perf and send S3 path to thread (due EOD)
- kevin: assemble trace bucket + flamegraphs and attach (due EOD)
- elaine: confirm routing rollback plan and runbook for next kernel rollout (due tomorrow)
- carla: prepare customer-facing incident note draft (due in 30m)
kevin: quick note: observed syscall latency cluster on `futex_wait` and `ksoftirqd` wakeups in upgraded hosts. Suspect scheduler heuristics or IRQ handling change in 5.15.73. Detailed flamegraphs will show if it's preempt or irqbound.
maria: adding a pinned hypothesis comment: "kernel IRQ/scheduler regression causing sporadic long preempt windows yielding p95 surge". We'll include perf counters, `dmesg` snippets, and trace buckets in RCA doc.
incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> partial (routing mitigation applied). Incident assigned to team: eng-sre. Severity downgraded to S2. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-4302
maria: thanks all — continuing collection and will open an RCA doc with timeline, hypothesis, artifacts, and final customer-impact summary. I'll post the doc link here when ready. :memo:
kevin: attaching quick commands we used for artifacts: ```
# trace gather
rdctl traces export --service=inference --from=2026-03-17T01:08:00Z --to=2026-03-17T01:22:00Z --out s3://redwood-incident/INC-2026-4302/traces.tar.gz
# perf capture (on hosts)
ssh root@i-0a1b2c 'perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 900; perf script | gzip > /var/tmp/perf-01-08-01-22.gz'
```
carla: draft customer message ready, will attach when doc has a clear RCA and timeline. For now informing affected accounts that we applied routing mitigation and are investigating root cause. :phone:
maria: closing pager channel for now, will reopen if we see regression. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
